question: Abdullah casts [Telemin Performance] targeting Nico. In response, Nico casts [Veil of Summer]. Abdullah responds with their own Veil of Summer. What happens?
judge_answer:
Abdullah's Veil of Summer resolves first. Then Nico's resolves and draws them a card. Then Telemin Performance tries to resolve and fails, since it has an illegal target.

(Abdullah's Veil of Summer didn't accomplish anything useful.)
mined_rationale: Resolution order is last-in-first-out (117.7/608.1), Veil of Summer's hexproof from blue and black makes Nico an illegal target for the blue Telemin Performance (702.11d), and a spell whose only target is illegal on resolution is removed from the stack without resolving (608.2b).

question: Alexis would like to choose colorless for [Regicide]. Can they?
judge_answer: No. Colorless is not a color.
mined_rationale: There are exactly five colors and colorless is the absence of color (105.1, 105.2, 105.2c); any of these states that colorless isn't a color Alexis could choose.

question: Aleah casts [Clash of Titans], can Aleah choose Nixon's [Storm Crow] for both targets?
judge_answer: No. The word "another" here retains its normal English meaning, and means that both targets cannot be the same creature.
mined_rationale: The CR has no rule defining 'another', so the closest citable basis is the targeting rule that otherwise would have let the same creature be chosen for both instances of 'target' (115.3/601.2c); the word 'another' overrides that in plain English.

question: Andre casts [Abrupt Decay] targeting Nico's 5/5 Horse creature token, then responds by targeting it with [Arcane Denial]. What happens?
judge_answer: Arcane Denial resolves but can't counter Abrupt Decay. During Nico's upkeep, Andre draws one to three cards, based on their choice.
mined_rationale: Abrupt Decay's 'can't be countered' ability functions on the stack and beats Arcane Denial's attempt to counter it (113.6g/101.2), Arcane Denial still does as much as it can (609.3) so its draw clauses apply, and those draws are delayed triggered abilities that happen at the next upkeep (603.7a).

question: Armani casts [Hangarback Walker] with X = 3. Can Neriah counter it with [Thoughtbind]?
judge_answer: No. The mana value of a spell is determined by adding together the symbols in the upper right corner of the card. The mana value of Hangarback Walker on the stack is 6.
mined_rationale: Mana value is the total mana in the mana cost (202.3), and while the spell is on the stack each X equals the announced value (202.3e/107.3a), so Hangarback Walker with X=3 has mana value 6 and dodges Thoughtbind.

question: Nikolas controls [Mindcrank]. Ari casts [Vampiric Tutor]. Will the card Ari put on top of their library get milled?
judge_answer: Yes. Mindcrank triggers during the resolution of Vampiric Tutor and will be put onto the stack after Vampiric Tutor finishes resolving. (Ari can cast an instant before the trigger resolves.)
mined_rationale: Mindcrank can trigger mid-resolution, but the trigger waits and goes on the stack the next time a player would receive priority, i.e. after Vampiric Tutor finishes resolving (117.2a, 603.3, 117.5 all state this); by then the tutored card is on top of the library and gets milled.

question: Does Nicole have a chance to cast [Surgical Extraction] after Addison has drawn for turn but before they have a chance to cast a sorcery?
judge_answer: Yes. Players receive priority in the draw step after a card has been drawn.
mined_rationale: The draw is a turn-based action at the start of the draw step (504.1) and the active player only then gets priority (504.2); both are needed to place Nicole's instant window after the draw but before any sorcery.

question: Amir casts [Archon of Cruelty], and before it resolves Norah casts [Surge of Salvation]. What happens when the Archon resolves?
judge_answer: Archon of Cruelty's ability triggers but is not placed onto the stack, since there are no legal targets for it. Amir will not draw a card or gain life.
mined_rationale: Surge of Salvation makes Norah an illegal choice for 'target opponent' (702.11c/702.11d), and a triggered ability with no legal choices for a required target is simply removed from the stack, so none of it happens - including the draw and lifegain (603.3d).

question: Nia controls [Hollowhenge Huntmaster]. Anders casts [Flesh Duplicate]. Can they have it enter the battlefield as a copy of Hollowhenge Huntmaster?
judge_answer: Yes. Hexproof prevents Hollowhenge Huntmaster from being the target of an opponent's spell or ability, but Flesh Duplicate doesn't target anything.
mined_rationale: Hexproof only stops the permanent from being the target of opponents' spells and abilities (702.11b), and being affected by a spell that never says 'target' isn't targeting (115.10a/115.10), so Flesh Duplicate can copy Hollowhenge Huntmaster.

question: Ariel controls [Rest in Peace] and targets Nataly's [Dauthi Voidwalker] with [Lightning Bolt]. What happens to each card?
judge_answer:
Ariel chooses whether Lightning Bolt goes to exile with or without a counter.

There are two replacement effects attempting to replace Lightning Bolt going to the graveyard with it going to exile, so its controller gets to choose which to apply.

Then state-based actions are checked and Dauthi Voidwalker is put into exile.
mined_rationale: Rest in Peace and Dauthi Voidwalker are two replacement effects competing over Lightning Bolt hitting the graveyard, so its controller picks which applies (616.1/616.1e); separately, the Voidwalker has lethal damage marked and is destroyed as a state-based action (704.5g) before being exiled.

question: Ari controls [Emeria Shepherd]. They play [Sacred Peaks], and target [Garenbrig Carver] in their graveyard. In response, Noelle activates [Alchemist's Refuge]. When that ability resolves, they casts [Blood Moon]. When Emeria Shepherd's ability resolves, where is Garenbrig Carver?
judge_answer:
Ari's hand.

Blood Moon changes Sacred Peaks's subtypes to "Mountain", and Sacred Peaks loses all other subtypes. During the resolution of the ability, Sacred Peaks is no longer a Plains and therefore Garenbrig Carver will not return to the battlefield.
mined_rationale: Blood Moon sets Sacred Peaks's subtype to Mountain, so it loses its other land types (305.7), and Emeria Shepherd's ability checks whether the land is a Plains when the ability resolves (608.2h) - it isn't, so Garenbrig Carver goes to hand.

question: Arjun controls [Thermopod] and has no cards in their graveyard. Assuming they have enough mana, can they activate [Molten-Tail Masticore]'s first activated ability?
judge_answer: Yes. Arjun first puts the ability onto the stack, after which it won't matter if Molten-Tail Masticore is on the battlefield anymore. Arjun then has a chance to activate mana abilities, at which point they can sacrifice Molten-Tail Masticore. Then Arjun pays the cost of the spell, exiling Molten-Tail Masticore from their graveyard.
mined_rationale: The activated ability goes on the stack and exists independently of Molten-Tail Masticore (602.2a/113.7a), and the player may activate mana abilities - sacrificing the Masticore to Thermopod - after that but before costs are paid (601.2g/601.2h), so it's in the graveyard in time to be exiled for the cost.

question: Can Ashley pay {B}{B}{B}{B}{B}{B} to cast [Beseech the Queen] or is Ashley limited to only paying {B}{B}{B} to do so?
judge_answer: After the first step of casting a spell, which is announcing it and moving it to the stack, Ashley makes choices regarding modes, alternative costs, additional costs, etc. This step includes deciding whether they will be paying {B} or {2} for each hybrid symbol ({2/B}) in Beseech the Queen's mana cost. They may always choose to cast it for {6} instead of {B}{B}{B} (or {2}{B}{B} or {4}{B}). Later on during the casting of the spell, the colorless parts of the mana cost may be paid with any color, including black.
mined_rationale: The nonhybrid equivalent of each {2/B} is announced during casting (601.2b), a monocolored hybrid symbol can be paid with one black or two mana of any type (107.4e), and generic mana in costs can be paid with any type of mana including black (107.4b) - so six black mana is legal.

question: Alfred casts [Stream of Thought], replicating it twice. Nico controls [Chalice of the Void] with 1 charge counter. What happens?
judge_answer: The original Stream of Thought is countered, the two copies resolve as normal. Replicate and Chalice of the Void both trigger when the spell is cast. Since the Chalice of the Void trigger is controlled by the player last in turn order, it will resolve first, countering Stream of Thought. Then Stream of Thought's trigger resolves and creates two copies of Stream of Thought. The copies are not cast, so they don't trigger Chalice of the Void.
mined_rationale: Ordering of the two cast-triggers on the stack comes from APNAP trigger placement (603.3b, or the general APNAP rule 101.4), and the copies dodging Chalice comes from 707.10 stating a copy of a spell isn't cast. Both required.

question: Amelia casts [Aminatou's Augury] exiling an artifact and an instant. Afterwards Amelia casts another Aminatou's Augury, which exiles an instant. Can they cast both instants?
judge_answer: Yes. Each Aminatou's Augury creates a separate effect that applies to cards it exiled. Casting an instant off the first Aminatou's Augury doesn't preclude Amelia from casting an instant off the second one.
mined_rationale: The answer rests on each resolution of Aminatou's Augury creating its own separate effect, so its 'a spell of each type' permission is tracked per effect; 609.1 is the only chunk that states a resolving spell creates effects of its own. Low confidence - the CR has no rule squarely on point.

question: Agustin casts [Seasoned Pyromancer] and has two other cards in hand, one of which is a land card. Nico controls [Leyline of the Void]. How many tokens are created?
judge_answer: One token is created. The cards discarded from hand can still be seen by Seasoned Pyromancer's effect even though going to the graveyard was replaced by going to exile.
mined_rationale: The discard still happens; only the destination is replaced, and 400.7j states that when an effect moves an object to a public zone (exile), other parts of that effect can still find it, which is why Seasoned Pyromancer counts the discarded cards.

question: Aranza controls a [Welding Jar] enchanted by Nico's [Curse Artifact]. In response to the trigger during Aranza's upkeep, Nico casts [Word of Seizing] to take control of the Welding Jar. What happens as the trigger resolves?
judge_answer: Aranza is dealt 2 damage. Sacrificing the Welding Jar is a cost. If the cost isn't paid, the default action of dealing 2 damage to Aranza happens. Aranza cannot sacrifice a permanent that they don't control.
mined_rationale: 701.21a states a player can't sacrifice a permanent they don't control, and 118.12a states that '[do something] unless [a player does something else]' means the default action happens when the optional action isn't taken. Both are needed to get to '2 damage'.

question: Aviana controls a [Meng Huo's Horde] and a [Deathrite Shaman]. Nico controls a [Propaganda]. Can Aviana use Deathrite Shaman's ability to pay for the Meng Huo's Horde to attack?
judge_answer: No. Propaganda imposes a cost on Meng Huo's Horde attacking, which must be paid as a part of declaring it as an attacker. Deathrite Shaman's ability is not a mana ability, so the last time it could be activated before attackers are declared is during the beginning of combat step. At the end of that step, the mana would empty from Aviana's mana pool.
mined_rationale: Three separate facts: the attack cost is determined and paid inside the declare attackers turn-based action (any of 508.1h/i/j), Deathrite Shaman's targeted ability isn't a mana ability so it can't be activated there (605.1a), and mana from the beginning of combat step is gone by then (106.4).

question: Ava controls [Undead Minotaur] enchanted with [Shade's Form]. Nico casts [Hour of Revelation] to destroy both Undead Minotaur and Shade's Form. Will Undead Minotaur return to the battlefield?
judge_answer: Yes. Shade's Form has a triggered ability that occurs when the enchanted permanent dies. For most triggers the game checks to see if they occur right after every event. However for "dies" triggers the game checks what the game state looked like right before they triggered to see if they trigger. In this case, checking right before Hour of Revelation resolved results in Shade's Form triggering and returning Undead Minotaur to the battlefield.
mined_rationale: Shade's Form's trigger is a leaves-the-battlefield/dies trigger, and the look-back-in-time exception is what makes it trigger off a mass destruction that also killed the Aura; 603.10 states the principle and 603.10a lists LTB abilities, so either one is a correct hit.

question: Amara controls [Muraganda Petroglyphs] and [Wayward Angel], and has more than 7 cards in their graveyard. Nehemiah casts and resolves [Humility]. What are Wayward Angel's characteristics?
judge_answer:
Wayward Angel is a Black, 6/6 creature with no abilities. The rest of its characteristics remain the same as printed on the card. 
Wayward Angel's threshold ability changes both its color, abilities, and P/T. Therefore, it applies in layers 5, 6, and 7 with the appropriate parts applying in their appropriate layers, and the layers are applied in order. Similarly, Humility's effect is applied in layers 6 and 7, as appropriate. 
Applying layers in order:
- In layer 5, Wayward Angel becomes black. 
- In layer 6 there are two contending effects: Wayward Angel's ability giving it trample and an upkeep triggered ability, and Humility's ability removing all abilities from Wayward Angel. There is no dependency between the two, since Wayward Angel's ability has already started applying in a previous layer, and will continue to apply even if removed by Humility's ability. The effects are then applied in timestamp order with Wayward Angel's ability applying first, since it has an earlier timestamp. So in layer 6, Wayward Angel first gains trample and "At the beginning of your upkeep, sacrifice a creature.", and then loses all abilities to Humility.
- In layer 7, P/T setting effects are applied first, so that Humility first turns Wayward Angel into a 1/1. Then effects modifying P/T are applied, of which there are two: Wayward Angel's own ability that, even though removed, continues to apply and gives it +3/+3, and Muraganda Petroglyphs's ability giving Wayward Angel +2/+2 since it now has no abilities. Wayward Angel's P/T is finally 6/6.
mined_rationale: The judge walks the layer system: layer order (613.1 and the layer 6/7 entries), the rule that an effect already applying keeps applying after its ability is removed (613.6), layer 7 sublayer order setting-before-modifying (613.4/b/c), timestamp order inside layer 6 (613.7), and the absence of a dependency (613.8a). Each is a distinct required step with interchangeable statements inside.

question: Amirah controls Azors Gateway with 4 different CMC cards exiled by it. They targets it with [Karn's Touch]. After that resolves, they activates [Azor's Gateway], and transforms it into [Sanctum of the Sun]. What are the characteristics of the new object after it has transformed?
judge_answer: Sanctum of the Sun is a 2/2 Legendary artifact creature land with the ability "{T}: Add X mana of any one color, where X is your life total". The requirement that Azor's Gateway be an artifact is part of the targeting restriction of the spell, after the spell resolves, it creates a continuous effect on the permanent that was targeted (in this case Azor's Gateway) that lasts until end of turn. When a double-faced card transforms it doesn't become a new object, and any effects that applied to it before the transformation will continue to apply afterwards.
mined_rationale: 712.18 states a double-faced permanent that transforms doesn't become a new object and effects applying to it keep applying - that is exactly why Karn's Touch's animation survives the transform into Sanctum of the Sun.

question: Amaris controls [Eruth, Tormented Prophet] and, during their draw step, they attempt to dredge [Golgari Grave-Troll]. What happens?
judge_answer: Amaris can dredge Golgari Grave-Troll instead of drawing. There are two replacement effects attempting to replace Amaris's draw. Since they are the affected player, they choose whether to exile the card with Eruth, Tormented Prophet or dredge with Golgari Grave-Troll. Once one of the replacement effects has been applied, the "draw" event no longer exists, and the other replacement effect does not apply.
mined_rationale: Dredge is a replacement effect for the draw (702.52a), and 616.1/616.1e state the affected player picks which competing replacement effect to apply, after which the draw event no longer exists for the other one.

question: Nicole controls [Oraxid]. Can Austin cast [First Volley] targeting Oraxid with [Evermind] spliced onto it?
judge_answer: No. Evermind has a color indicator making it blue, which is not granted by splice since it's not part of the card's text.
mined_rationale: Splice only adds the spliced card's rules text to the spell (702.47a), and Evermind's blue comes from a color indicator, which is a separate characteristic rather than rules text (204.2). Both are needed for 'the spell doesn't become blue'.

question: In a game of commander, Natasha has shuffled their commander into their library. Adan casts [Praetor's Grasp] targeting Natasha and finds Natasha's commander. Can Natasha choose to put it into the command zone?
judge_answer: Yes. Despite being face-down, it's still Natasha's commander, and they can choose to have it move to the command zone as a state-based action.
mined_rationale: 903.9a states a commander that was put into exile may be moved to the command zone by its owner as a state-based action, which is the whole answer regardless of the card being face down.

question: Alex controls [Rhythm of the Wild], [Grumgully, the Generous], [Renata, Called to the Hunt], and [Hardened Scales]. Alex then casts [Grizzled Outrider]. If they chooses to put a counter on Grizzled Outrider for Rhythm of the Wild, how many +1/+1 counters will it enter with in total?
judge_answer: Four. Every card on the battlefield has a replacement effect that modifies how Grizzled Outrider will enter the battlefield. When applying replacement effects, each effect has a chance to apply once and only once, so even though Alex can choose which order to apply the effects in, Hardened Scales will only get one chance to modify how many counters Grizzled Outrider enters the battlefield with, and will only ever add one additional counter.
mined_rationale: The controller chooses the order of the competing enters-with-counters replacement effects (616.1/616.1e/616.1f), but 614.5 states a replacement effect only gets one opportunity, so Hardened Scales can only add one counter. Both halves required.

question: Ann has a [Sphere of Resistance], a Plains and a Swamp. Can Ann cast [Prismatic Ending] targeting [Drake Familiar]?
judge_answer: Yes Ann can cast Prismatic Ending targeting Drake Familiar. Ann can target Drake Familiar regardless of whether the final spell will exile it or not, as any card is targetable with Prismatic Ending, and it's only exiled if the conditions are met. Then Ann chooses the value of X, in this case they can select 0, then add Sphere of Resistance's tax resulting in a required mana payment of two. If Ann chooses to use two different colors of mana, when the spell resolves it will see that two colors were spent and exile the target if it's mana value is two or less.
mined_rationale: X is announced while casting (601.2b) and Sphere of Resistance's increase is added when the total cost is determined and locked in (601.2f), giving the two-mana payment that lets two colors be spent. Targeting is unrestricted, so no separate target rule is required.

question: Abram attacks with [Robber of the Rich], exiling [Skewer the Critics] from Nico's library. Can Abram pay Skewer the Critics's Spectacle cost with only {C}?
judge_answer:
Yes.

Robber of the Rich allows Abram to cast the card and "may spend mana as though it were mana of any color to cast that spell." This changes how the player may pay a cost, and they can do so with any mana, regardless of color. 

"Spectacle" is an alternative cost ([702.137a]), and can only be used if no other alternative cost is being paid. Luckily, Robber of the Rich does not create an alternative cost, it just changes how mana may be spent.
mined_rationale: 609.4b states 'spend mana as though it were mana of any color' only changes how a cost may be paid and isn't an alternative cost, and 702.137a states spectacle is an alternative cost. Both needed to conclude the two don't conflict.

question: Alex controls [Obosh, the Preypiercer] and casts their last card, [Flame Spill], targeting a 1/1 creature that Nevaeh controls. How much damage will Nevaeh take?
judge_answer: Six. First Alex will allocate one damage to the token and three to Nevaeh. Obosh, the Preypiercer's replacement effect will then double the three damage being dealt to Nevaeh to six.
mined_rationale: The 1/3 split is announced as the spell is cast (601.2d), and Obosh's 'instead' doubling is a replacement effect (614.1a) that applies to the three damage headed for Nevaeh, making it six.

question: Alessandro activates [Inkmoth Nexus] to turn it into a creature and attacks Noor with it. Noor doesn't block it and then casts [Through the Breach], putting [Melira, Sylvok Outcast] onto the battlefield. What happens during the combat damage step?
judge_answer:
Inkmoth Nexus's ability gives it infect, and Melira, Sylvok Outcast's effect makes it lose infect. The effects are applied in timestamp order, so Inkmoth Nexus does not have infect. Noor will lose 1 life when damage is dealt.

(There is no dependency here because neither effect changes the text or the existence of the other, what it applies to, or what it does to any of the things it applies to.)
mined_rationale: The grant and the removal of infect are both layer 6 effects applied in timestamp order (613.7/613.7b), and the judge's parenthetical is the dependency test failing (613.8a). Both required.

question: Autumn controls [Jibbirik Omnivore], a token copy of Jibbirik Omnivore produced by [Stolen Identity], a 1/1 Saproling token created by [Morbid Bloom], [Moonscarred Werewolf], and a token copy of Moonscarred Werewolf produced by [Twinflame]. Nash casts [Ratchet Bomb] and activates its second ability. As Ratchet Bomb's ability resolves, what is destroyed?
judge_answer: The Saproling token and the token copy of Moonscarred Werewolf. Copy effects copy mana cost, so the token Jibbirik Omnivore doesn't have a mana value of 0. Tokens that are created by an effect that sets their characteristics only have those characteristics. The Saproling token has no mana cost, so its mana value is 0. The mana value of transformed transforming double-faced cards is determined by their front face, so the Moonscarred Werewolf isn't destroyed. Copies of double-faced cards have a mana value of 0.
mined_rationale: Four separate mana-value facts the answer needs: copies copy mana cost (707.2), a token has only the characteristics its creating effect defines so it has no mana cost (111.3), an object with no mana cost has mana value 0 (202.3a), and a transformed nonmodal double-faced permanent uses its front face while a copy of a back face is 0 (202.3b).

question: Alex casts [Brainstorm] using the ability of [Jace, Telepath Unbound]. Nina casts [Memory Lapse] and counters Brainstorm. Where does Brainstorm go?
judge_answer:
Alex's library.

Two replacement effects are trying to replace the same event. Since Memory Lapse's effect is a self-replacement effect, it applies first. Once it's applied, Brainstorm is moving to the library and Jace, Telepath Unbound's effect no longer applies.
mined_rationale: Memory Lapse's 'put it on top of its owner's library instead' is a self-replacement effect, and both 614.15 and 616.1a state self-replacement effects are applied before other replacement effects; either chunk answers it.

question: Nathalia controls [Welding Jar] and [Duskworker]. Ariel casts [Prismari Command], choosing the "deal 2 damage" and "destroy target artifact" modes, targeting Duskworker with both. In response, Nathalia activates Welding Jar's ability targeting Duskworker. What happens?
judge_answer: Duskworker will end up tapped and have no damage marked on it. Welding Jar's ability will resolve first, regenerating Duskworker. When Prismari Command resolves, the game carries out the instructions in the order written. First, Prismari Command deals 2 damage to Duskworker. The replacement effect generated by the regeneration ability will not apply yet, as even though Duskworker has been dealt lethal damage, it would only be destroyed when state-based actions are checked, and state-based actions are checked when a player would get priority. Next Prismari Command tries to destroy Duskworker and the replacement effect applies, replacing the destruction event with Duskworker being tapped and having all damaged marked on it removed. Lastly Prismari Command finishes resolving and leaves the stack and state-based actions are checked. Since Duskworker no longer has any damage marked on it, it will not be die.
mined_rationale: Regeneration is a shield that replaces the next destruction and taps the creature and removes damage (701.19a), destruction from lethal damage only happens when SBAs are checked, which is when a player would get priority (704.3), and Prismari Command's modes happen in written order (608.2c). All three required.

question: Armando controls [Mana Reflection] and taps [Pyromancer's Goggles] to add {R}{R}. They spend one mana to cast [Into the Fray]. Later in the phase they spend the other mana to cast [Galvanic Discharge]. Which one(s) are copied?
judge_answer: Both are copied. Mana Reflection has a replacement effect that changes the amount of mana produced by Pyromancer's Goggles. A separate delayed trigger is created for each mana.
mined_rationale: 106.6a states that when a replacement effect increases the mana produced, a separate delayed triggered ability is created for each mana produced - exactly the Mana Reflection plus Pyromancer's Goggles case.

question: Autumn restarts the game with [Karn Liberated]'s last ability. They put a [Quilled Slagwurm] onto the battlefield as it resolves. Can it attack on their first turn?
judge_answer: Yes. Karn's ability finishes resolving just before the first turn's untap step, so the creature has been controlled continuously since the turn began and can attack.
mined_rationale: The attack question is the summoning sickness rule, which asks whether the creature has been controlled continuously since the turn began (302.6); 727.1 supplies that Karn's ability restarts the game and a new game begins with that player's turn, so the creature is there before the turn starts.

question: Abraham controls [Drought] and [Derelor]. How many Swamps would they have to sacrifice in order to cast a [Virulent Wound]?
judge_answer: 1. The mana cost of a spell doesn't change, regardless of what was paid for it.
mined_rationale: Drought counts {B} symbols in the spell's mana cost, which is what's printed on the card (202.1/202.1a); 601.2f states cost increases like Derelor's are part of the total cost, not the mana cost. Any of these states that what was paid doesn't change the mana cost.

question: Abram controls a [Blood Moon], a [Life and Limb], and a [Tropical Island], that entered the battlefield in that order. Is the Tropical Island a creature?
judge_answer: No. Applying Blood Moon's effect first would prevent Life and Limb's effect from applying to Tropical Island and applying Life and Limb's effect first would not affect how Blood Moon's effect is applied or what it does, so Life and Limb's effect is dependent on Blood Moon's effect and waits to apply until afterwards. Since Blood Moon's effect makes Tropical Island no longer a Forest, Life and Limb doesn't apply to it at all.
mined_rationale: Both effects are type-changing and so share layer 4 (613.1d), which is a precondition of dependency; 613.8a defines the dependency test the judge runs and 613.8b states the dependent effect waits, so Blood Moon applies first and Life and Limb never applies.

question: Nixon has a [Southern Elephant] and a [Skullbriar, the Walking Grave] with 3 +1/+1 counters in their graveyard. Addison casts [Ghastly Conscription], targeting Nixon. What happens to the counters on the Skullbriar, the Walking Grave? Will Nixon know which manifested card is which?
judge_answer: When in the graveyard, Skullbriar, the Walking Grave had the ability that allowed it to keep its counters, so it is exiled and shuffled with 3 +1/+1 counters. When it's moved to the battlefield, it's face down and no longer has that ability, so the counters cease to exist. It had the counters immediately before entering the battlefield however, so Nixon will know which face-down permanent is the Skullbriar, the Walking Grave and which is the Southern Elephant.
mined_rationale: 122.2 states counters cease to exist on a zone change (Skullbriar's own ability is the exception while it has it), and manifesting makes it a face-down 2/2 with no text (701.40a, restated by 708.2/708.2a), so the ability is gone and the counters vanish as it enters.

question: Asa controls [Library of Leng] and is discarding a card due to [Azra Oddsmaker]'s ability. Can they put the discarded card on top of their library? If so, what happens?
judge_answer: Yes. Discarding a cost to the ability is a cost [118.12], but that doesn't stop it from being an effect as well. Library of Leng only changes where the card moves to, not that it was discarded, so the cost was paid and the remainder of Azra Oddsmaker's ability will resolve as normal.
mined_rationale: 118.12 makes 'discard a card. If you do' a cost paid on resolution, and 118.11 says a cost whose actions are modified by another effect is still paid (701.9c likewise treats a discard redirected to a hidden zone as a discard that can pay a cost). Both halves are needed: the cost framing plus the rule that Library of Leng's redirection doesn't undo payment.

question: Noor controls [Rhystic Study]. Alex casts [Mishra's Domination]. As Rhystic Study's trigger resolves, who makes their choice first? Does Noor choose whether or not to draw a card, and if yes, Alex may pay the mana to prevent it? Or does Alex choose to pay the mana first, and if they don't, Noor has the choice to draw a card?
judge_answer: Alex chooses first.
mined_rationale: 118.12a converts 'you may draw a card unless that player pays {1}' into 'that player may pay {1}; if they don't, you may draw', which directly establishes that the paying player chooses first.

question: Albert, Brielle, and Campbell are playing a multiplayer game. Brielle controls [Stalking Leonin]. Albert casts [Worst Fears] to take control of Brielle's next turn. After Brielle begins their turn, can Albert see which player was chosen for the Stalking Leonin?
judge_answer: No. The choice was made as Stalking Leonin entered the battlefield, which already happened- it's no longer visible to Brielle. Albert can choose to activate the ability (at which point all players will know who was chosen), but otherwise the choice is not visible to any player.
mined_rationale: 723.4 is the only rule governing what a player controlling another player can see: only information that would currently be visible to the controlled player. A choice already made secretly isn't such information, so Albert can't see it.

question: Abdullah controls [Primal Vigor] and casts [Rescuer Sphinx], choosing to return Primal Vigor to their hand. How many +1/+1 counters will Rescuer Sphinx enter the battlefield with?
judge_answer: Two. Both cards have a replacement effect. Abdullah will choose whether they are returning a permanent, but won't actually complete the action until Rescuer Sphinx enters the battlefield. Therefore Primal Vigor will still apply to the +1/+1 counter being from Rescuer Sphinx's ability.
mined_rationale: The as-enters replacement's choice is made before the permanent enters and the bounce it causes happens as part of that same entry event (614.12/614.12a/614.13a), so Primal Vigor is still on the battlefield; 614.16/616.1 then make Primal Vigor's counter-doubling apply to the counter placed by the Sphinx's own replacement effect.

question: Addison has six cards in their graveyard and casts [Epicenter] targeting Nataly. In response, Nataly casts [Blossoming Calm]. Before it resolves, Addison casts [Dampen Thought] targeting themself. What happens?
judge_answer: Neither player will sacrifice any lands. The text on Epicenter is a self-replacement effect and changes what the spell is doing. However, before the replacement effect would be applied the game checks to see if all the targets for the spell are still legal. Nataly is no longer a legal target, therefore the spell won't resolve.
mined_rationale: 608.2b is the whole answer: target legality is checked first on resolution, and a spell whose every target is illegal doesn't resolve at all, so neither the normal effect nor the threshold self-replacement happens.

question: Aislinn controls [Anointed Procession] and a [Skullmulcher]. They cast [Tempt with Reflections] targeting the Skullmulcher. Can Aislinn apply the devour replacement effect before the Anointed Procession replacement effect, sacrificing 1 creature to have each token enter with a +1/+1 counter?
judge_answer: No. There are two replacement effects trying to apply to the original event of creating a Skullmulcher: Skullmulcher's own effect and Anointed Procession's effect. Skullmulcher's effect applies to it entering the battlefield however, while Anointed Procession's effect applies to it being created, so Anointed Procession's effect must be applied first. After that is applied the original Skullmulcher's effect doesn't exist anymore, but each of the new Skullmulchers entering the battlefield has its own effect, which can now be applied individually.
mined_rationale: 616.1g is exactly this case: entering the battlefield is an event contained within creating the token, so the token-doubling effect must be applied before any of the entering-the-battlefield replacements (its example uses Doubling Season plus an as-enters choice).

question: Bailey controls [Pandemonium]. Anderson casts [Gray Ogre] and targets Bailey's [Jibbirik Omnivore] with the Pandemonium trigger. In response Chelsea casts [Incinerate] targeting Anderson causing them to lose the game. Will Bailey's creature die?
judge_answer: The triggered ability of Pandemonium includes a choice to be made upon resolution. However the player that is supposed to make that choice is no longer in the game, therefore the controller of the trigger chooses another player to make that choice. In this case Bailey will choose another player to decide whether Pandemonium's trigger will deal damage to Jibbirik Omnivore. Bailey is the controller of the trigger since they control the enchantment that generated the trigger, even though Anderson is the player making choices about the trigger.
mined_rationale: 800.4g states that when an object requires a departed player to make a choice other than paying a cost, the object's controller picks another player to make it; 603.3a/113.8 establish that Bailey, who controlled Pandemonium when it triggered, controls the ability and therefore makes that pick.

question: Alice controls a [Life and Limb], a [Blood Moon], and a 1/1 Green Saproling Creature token, that entered the battlefield in that order. What is the Saproling?
judge_answer: It's a 1/1 green Land Creature - Mountain Saproling with "{T}: Add {R}.". Applying Life and Limb's effect would allow Blood Moon's effect to apply to the Saproling and applying Blood Moon's effect first would not affect how Life and Limb's effect is applied or what it does, so Blood Moon's effect is dependent on Life and Limb's effect and waits to apply until afterwards. Since Life and Limb's effect makes the Saproling a nonbasic land, Blood Moon then applies and turns it into a Mountain with "{T}: Add {R}." and no other abilities.
mined_rationale: 613.8a defines dependency (Life and Limb's effect changes what Blood Moon's effect applies to, but not vice versa) and 613.8b says the dependent effect waits until afterward, overriding timestamps. Both halves are needed to get the Mountain Saproling.

question: Alfredo controls [Magnetic Web] and is attacking with two [Knight Errant]s with magnet counters on them. Nico controls one [Soaring Drake] that also has a magnet counter on it. What are Nico's legal blocks?
judge_answer: Nico can block either Knight Errant with their Magnetic Web. When declaring blockers, Nico must fulfill the maximum number of requirements, while not violating any restrictions.
mined_rationale: 509.1c is the blocking-requirement rule: the defending player must obey the maximum possible number of requirements without violating restrictions, so with one legal blocker Nico satisfies exactly one of the two 'block that creature' requirements and may choose which.

question: At the beginning of the game, Alianna announced [Zirda, the Dawnwaker] as their companion. During the game, Alianna cast [Glistening Goremonger] from their sideboard with [Wish]. Later, Alianna restarts the game with [Karn Liberated]. What happens?
judge_answer: Glistening Goremonger will be shuffled into Alianna's library along with the rest of the cards in the game. Because Glistening Goremonger violates Zirda, the Dawnwaker's companion restriction, Alianna can't announce it as their companion for the restarted game.
mined_rationale: 727.2 puts every card involved in the ended game (including the wished-for card) into the new game, so Goremonger is shuffled into the library; 702.139a/103.2b (and 727.1, which sends the restart through rule 103) require the companion condition to be met by the new starting deck, which it now isn't.

question: Avery controls [Wayward Angel] and has 7 cards in their graveyard. Nathan casts [Turn to Frog], targeting Wayward Angel. What are Wayward Angel's characteristics after Turn to Frog resolves?
judge_answer: It's a 4/4 blue Frog with no abilities. Wayward Angel's last ability begins to apply in layer 5. It's removed by Turn to Frog in layer 6, but since it's already started to apply, it will continue doing so in later layers. Wayward Angel has the earlier timestamp, so it gives itself trample and "At the beginning of your upkeep, sacrifice a creature" before Turn to Frog removes its abilities in layer 6.
mined_rationale: 613.6 is load-bearing: the threshold effect starts applying in layer 5 and keeps applying in layers 6 and 7 even though the ability generating it is removed. The layer assignments (613.1e-g) and timestamp order (613.7/613.7a/613.7b) are needed to see that Turn to Frog's later color change and ability removal win.

question: Autumn, Bethany, and Chaim started playing a multiplayer game. Chaim lost the game, and then Autumn restarted the game with [Karn Liberated]. Will Autumn draw a card on the first turn of the restarted game?
judge_answer: No. The game began with 2 players, so it is a two-player game.. Autumn will skip their draw step.
mined_rationale: 727.1 restarts with only the players still in the game (two), 800.1 defines a multiplayer game as one that begins with more than two players so the new game isn't one, and 103.8a then makes the starting player skip their first draw step.

question: Addison casts [Virulent Wound], targeting Natalee's [Memnite]. In response, Natalee casts [Resounding Roar] on the Memnite. What happens at the end of the turn?
judge_answer: The effect from Resounding Roar wears off, but the -1/-1 counter remains. Memnite dies. The delayed triggered ability created by Virulent Wound is not a continuous effect, so it still exists during the cleanup step, and will trigger due to Memnite dying. Natalee gets a poison counter.
mined_rationale: 514.2 ends the +4/+4 in cleanup while leaving the -1/-1 counter, 704.5f puts the now-0-toughness Memnite into the graveyard, 514.3a is what lets state-based actions and waiting triggers happen during the cleanup step, and 603.7b is the delayed trigger firing the next time its event occurs.

question: Amaris, Blaine, and Clyde begin a multiplayer game. In Amaris's upkeep, they use [Leyline of Anticipation], several [Simian Spirit Guide]s and [Desperate Ritual]s, and [Goblin Charbelcher] to kill Blaine. Does Amaris draw a card for the turn?
judge_answer: Yes. The game began with more than 2 players, so it is a multiplayer game, regardless of the current number of players remaining.. Amaris will draw a card during their draw step.
mined_rationale: 800.1 fixes multiplayer status at the game's start (more than two players), regardless of eliminations, and 103.8c/800.7 state that in multiplayer games other than Two-Headed Giant no player skips their first draw step.

question: Anya activates [Deceptive Landscape]. Before that resolves Nico casts [Aven Mindcensor]. When Anya is resolving Deceptive Landscape's ability, they find [Panglacial Wurm] in the top four cards of their library. Can they cast it?
judge_answer: Yes. Aven Mindcensor's ability is a replacement effect that replaces searching a library with searching only the top four cards of that library. However for the purposes of Panglacial Wurm's effect, it still qualifies as "searching a library".
mined_rationale: 701.23f states that when searching a zone is replaced with searching a portion of it, any other instructions referring to searching that zone still apply — so Panglacial Wurm's 'while you're searching your library' is satisfied.

question: Aimee controls a manifested [Wayward Angel] and has 7 cards in their graveyard. Noah casts [Turn to Frog], targeting Wayward Angel. After that resolves, Aimee turns Wayward Angel face up. What are Wayward Angel's characteristics afterwards?
judge_answer: It's a 4/4 black Frog with trample and "At the beginning of your upkeep, sacrifice a creature", but no other abilities. Wayward Angel receives a new timestamp when it turns face up, so its ability is applied before Turn to Frog in each layer. Wayward Angel's last ability is removed by Turn to Frog in layer 6, but since it's already started to apply in layer 5 to change its color to black, it will continue doing so in later layers. Turn to Frog has the earlier timestamp, so it makes Wayward Angel blue before it becomes black in layer 5 and removes Wayward Angel's abilities in layer 6 before it gains trample and "At the beginning of your upkeep, sacrifice a creature".
mined_rationale: 613.7f gives the permanent a new timestamp when it turns face up, putting Wayward Angel's ability after Turn to Frog; 613.7 supplies earlier-timestamp-first ordering, and 613.6 keeps the threshold effect applying in layers 6 and 7 even after Turn to Frog removes the ability in layer 6.

question: Alaia controls [Panharmonicon] and [Mycosynth Lattice] and has [Minotaur Warrior] and [Ogre Resister] in their graveyard. They cast [Dance of the Dead] targeting Minotaur Warrior. What happens as it enters the battlefield?
judge_answer: Dance of the Dead enters the battlefield attached to Minotaur Warrior and triggers twice. The first trigger will return Minotaur Warrior to the battlefield. The second trigger just does the same things again, so it has no relevant result.
mined_rationale: 603.2d handles an effect making a triggered ability trigger an additional time (Panharmonicon sees the Aura as an artifact entering), 603.4 has each copy recheck the intervening 'if it's on the battlefield' on resolution, and 701.3b/609.3 make the second resolution a no-op since the Aura is already attached and the creature card has left the graveyard.

question: Adelaide casts a [Keldon Champion]. In response, Nico casts [Hallow], targeting the Keldon Champion. When Adelaide attacks with the Keldon Champion that turn, will the damage be prevented?
judge_answer: Yes. Effects that apply to damage from a spell on the stack continue to apply to damage from the permanent that spell becomes.
mined_rationale: 609.7a states that if a permanent spell is chosen as the damage source, the effect applies to damage dealt by that spell and by the permanent it becomes — so Hallow's prevention still covers Keldon Champion's combat damage.

question: Ariel controls [Soul Seizer] (back face [Ghastly Haunting])which has been mutated with [Everquill Phoenix]. Everquill Phoenix is the top component. Naomi controls [Axegrinder Giant]. Ariel then attacks Naomi with the merged permanent. Naomi declared no blockers and the merged permanent deals damage to Naomi. What happens when the transformation trigger resolves if Ariel elects to transform the merged permanent and targets Axegrinder Giant?
judge_answer:
The component that consists of Soul Seizer is transformed. The merged permanent is still a creature. It is not attached to anything. The merged permanent has the abilities in the text box of the back half of Soul Seizer instead of the front half.

When Ariel chooses to transform the merged permanent, all double-faced components are transformed. The merged permanent now has the abilities of the back half of Soul Seizer instead of the front half. ([702.140e]) The merged permanent is still a creature as Everquill Phoenix is still the topmost card. When the transformation trigger tries to attach the merged permanent to Axegrinder Giant, it can't attach because the merged permanent is still a creature. It remains on the battlefield because the state-based action that puts auras not attached to anything into the graveyard is looking for the "Aura" subtype, not the "Enchant" keyword.
mined_rationale: 730.2i transforms every double-faced component of the merged permanent; 702.140e/730.2a keep it a creature with the topmost card's characteristics plus all components' abilities; 303.4d/701.3b stop the attach because a creature can't enchant anything; and 704.5m is the state-based action that checks for the Aura subtype, which the merged permanent doesn't have, so it stays.

question: Aubrey controls a [Gaea's Liege], [Rhonas the Indomitable], and 1 [Forest]. Noel controls 5 Forest. Can Aubrey attack with the Gaea's Liege and Rhonas the Indomitable?
judge_answer: No. All creatures are declared as attackers at the same time. Checking to see if any restrictions affect a potentially-attacking creature is done before the creature becomes an "attacking creature".
mined_rationale: 508.1c checks restrictions (Rhonas's 'can't attack unless') during the declaration, while 508.1k shows the chosen creatures don't become attacking creatures until after those checks (508.1a: all attackers chosen at once), so Gaea's Liege still has its non-attacking power at that moment.

question: Aurora controls a [Gaea's Liege] and 3 [Snow-Covered Forest]s. Nico controls a [Reverence] and 1 Snow-Covered Forest. Can Aurora attack with the Gaea's Liege?
judge_answer: Yes. Checking to see if any restrictions affect a potentially-attacking creature is done before the creature becomes an "attacking creature".
mined_rationale: 508.1c checks Reverence's restriction during the declaration of attackers, and 508.1k/508.1a establish that the creature doesn't become an attacking creature until after that check, so Gaea's Liege is still power 3 (Aurora's Forests) when the restriction is evaluated.

question: Amari has [Phyrexian Hulk] and [The Mimeoplasm] in their graveyard. Amari casts [Rise of the Dark Realms] to return both to the battlefield. Can they have The Mimeoplasm enter the battlefield as a copy of Phyrexian Hulk?
judge_answer: No. The Mimeoplasm has a replacement effect that modifies how it enters the battlefield. The game checks for any replacement effects that modify how an object will enter the battlefield before the object has changed zones. So Phyrexian Hulk is still in the graveyard while Amari is making choices for The Mimeoplasm, however they are not allowed to choose an object that is also changing zones at the same time.
mined_rationale: 614.12/614.12a have the as-enters choices made before The Mimeoplasm enters (so Phyrexian Hulk is still in the graveyard), while 614.13a forbids choosing an object that's entering the battlefield at the same time.

question: Autumn casts [Time Stretch]. Can they choose to skip both extra turns with [Time Vault]?
judge_answer: Yes. As their turn ends, they can apply Time Vault's replacement effect, which means the next turn gets skipped and Time Vault gets untapped as part of the next turn that actually happens. Then, since it's still tapped as Autumn's turn is ending, they can choose to skip the next turn again.
mined_rationale: 500.7 adds the two extra turns directly after the current one, and 614.10/614.10b handle the skip: skipping is a replacement effect, and the accompanying action (untapping Time Vault) happens as the first thing in the next turn that actually occurs, which is why it can be tapped again in time to skip the second extra turn.

question: Averie attacks with [Pristine Angel]. While it's tapped, Nico activates [Cephalid Snitch]'s ability targeting Pristine Angel. After that resolves, Averie casts a spell and untaps Pristine Angel. Can Nico now target the Pristine Angel with [Mob]?
judge_answer:
Yes. "Protection from all colors" is shorthand for protection from each color individually. It loses protection from black, and still has protection from all the other colors.

(The timestamp of Pristine Angel's ability does not change when it becomes untapped.)
mined_rationale: 702.16h (with 702.16g) states that 'protection from each [characteristic]' is shorthand for separate protection abilities, so losing protection from black leaves the others intact; 702.16b supplies the fact that protection is what was blocking targeting.
